delimitation_of_record: Primary stratum = the Eteocypriot-defining inscriptions of Amathus, per Perna 2015's delimitation as carried in the proposal (section 3.4). The reference corpus behind the delimitation (Egetmeyer's Woerterbuch, as counted by Duhoux 2009) holds 23 records (Cyprus and Egypt), 585 syllabograms, 540 identified, 49 distinct signs attested. Golgoi is a separate stratum and is never merged into the primary stratum (sensitivity S2 only). Merely-uninterpreted syllabic texts are not Eteocypriot by default. Beyond the items itemized in this file, the individual texts of the remaining primary-stratum inscriptions were not obtained at execution; they stand in the held-out set by delimitation, sealed.

inscriptions.date: Second half of the 4th century BCE (Sittig, on script; Mitford: shortly after the expulsion of Androkles, 312/311 BCE). The 'ca. 600 BC' date in popular sources is wrong and is not carried.
inscriptions.edition_of_record: Masson, Les inscriptions chypriotes syllabiques, no. 196 (2nd ed. 1983, pp. 206-209)

greek_side.sense: The city of the Amathusians (honours) Ariston, son of Aristonax, of noble birth. The Eteocypriot version is roughly twice the Greek version's length and broadly corresponds to it; it is not a literal translation (Masson, ICS p. 207).

inscriptions.label: ICS 196, the Amathus bilingual
inscriptions.object: Black marble slab (statue base), found in an antique shop at Limassol (Amathus district) 1913/14; published by Sittig 1914 from a photograph; the stone is lost thereafter, possibly in transport to America.
reading_variants_carried: Line 1 segment 2: the edition of record reads ma-to-ri; a minority popular treatment (Ancient Origins) argues the third sign should read we (we-to-ri). The variant is recorded, not adopted; the analysis uses the edition of record.
Line 2 segment 2: the two damaged signs are unread in the edition of record (Duhoux 2009 prints them as unread). Gordon's conjecture ku-no for them is recorded as a conjecture, not adopted.
sources_consulted: Wikipedia, 'Eteocypriot language' (CC BY-SA), reproducing Masson's text
Woudhuizen 2012, 'The Amathus Bilingual Inscription' (concordant with Masson)

inscriptions.date: 320-311 BCE (SEG 32.1318); Androkles, last king of Amathus.
inscriptions.edition_of_record: Hermary & Masson 1982, 'Inscriptions d'Amathonte IV', Bulletin de Correspondance Hellenique 106, pp. 235-244, no. 66; SEG 32.1318 A
inscriptions.eteocypriot_side_status: NOT OBTAINED. The Eteocypriot (syllabic) side exists but is very mutilated in the edition of record, and its sign-level transcription (Hermary & Masson 1982, pp. 236-238) could not be extracted through the lawful access route available at execution (Persee full text is served page-wise as page images; the transcription pages were not text-accessible). No sign of this side is held, and none is reconstructed here.

greek_side.note: The verbatim Greek wording is not transcribed: the open route consulted (attalus.org) presents the SEG translation, and the edition's Greek text was not text-accessible. No analysis in this study consumes the Greek wording of this item; the name ground truth is foreknowledge of record (preregistration section 2).
greek_side.translation_of_record: King [Androkles dedicated these images of his sons] Orestheus and Andragoras to Cyprian Aphrodite.

Hermary & Masson 1982, p. 235 (Persee open access, consulted)
PhilPapers abstract of record for the edition: the syllabic part is 'malheureusement tres mutilée' (very mutilated)

inscriptions.label: ICS 217, the Idalion tablet (Greek syllabic control)
inscriptions.object: Bronze tablet, Idalion, 5th century BCE; Bibliotheque nationale de France. Greek (Arcadocypriot dialect) written in the Cypriot syllabary: the control population's anchor text (same signary, known language).
sources_consulted: Wikipedia, 'Idalion Tablet' (CC BY-SA), reproducing Chadwick 1987's transliteration of face A, lines 3-4
inscriptions.status_note: PARTIAL: an excerpt (65 signs) of the full tablet is held. The control's registered role is the comparison rate for E2 scoring (preregistration sections 3.4, 4/P2); the full control corpus was not obtained at execution. No E1 pairing is administrable on this item (it is monolingual; no alphabetic Greek parallel side is held).

inscriptions.date: Probably 4th century BCE (ICS, p. 85, via Duhoux 2009).
inscriptions.edition_of_record: Perna 2019, preliminary report in BCH Supplement 60 (Cannavo & Thely eds., Les royaumes de Chypre a l'epreuve de l'histoire, pp. 213-220): a completely new edition from autopsy in the Louvre; 48 of 216 signs read differently from Masson, altering 24 words; the resulting reading is printed at a glance on p. 220. Perna 2019 supersedes Masson for this inscription (Egetmeyer 2016-2020 report).
inscriptions.label: ICS 194 + ICS 195, the great Amathus inscription (one stone, two engravers)
inscriptions.object: Stone inscription reused in a tomb, Amathus; ICS 194 and ICS 195 are two faces/hands of one stone (Duhoux 2009); probably 4th century BCE. 216 signs in Perna 2019's count.

licensing_basis: The ancient texts are uncopyrighted. What is transcribed here is the ancient text only, with citation of the edition of record; no edition apparatus, commentary, translation under copyright, or scan is reproduced. Open reproductions consulted are CC BY-SA (Wikipedia) or publisher open access (Persee, OpenEdition) or public-domain scholarship (Duhoux 2009 as published in Kadmos, consulted on academia.edu).
orientation_basis: Eteocypriot lines are written right-to-left (retrograde); segment and sign order in this file is reading order (orientation carried as data, per C095-10). Greek alphabetic sides are left-to-right.
signary_frame: Common syllabary (the primary stratum's frame). The Paphian signary is carried as a named variant frame only; no Paphian-stratum inscription is intaken into the primary stratum. Sign values are settled (Idalion bilingual, Phoenician-Greek: sign-value evidence only, never Eteocypriot evidence, per the contamination rule C095-7 and proposal section 4.1).
study: Eteocypriot Program, Spec 096 (execution commissioned 2026-11-20; founded on the Spec 095 Stage 5 scoping record of 2026-11-17)
transliteration_scheme: Cypriot syllabary sign values (Common syllabary frame), syllabograms hyphen-joined inside a segment; segments are the edition's word-divider-separated sequences, in reading order. Token conventions: a plain token is a legible sign; '[x]' is a sign restored by the edition; '?' is a damaged or illegible sign whose value the edition of record does not read.
